docRequirement: third-party-integrations.md:327 binds us to an organization-wide CLAUDE.md tier read from system directories — `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md` (macOS), `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md` (Linux and WSL), `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md` (Windows) — "for company-wide standards". memory.md:58 specifies its semantics as the **Managed policy** row of the load-order table: it is the broadest scope, so it is loaded BEFORE user and project CLAUDE.md, it is "Shared with: All users in organization", and memory.md:336 makes it un-excludable — "Managed policy CLAUDE.md files cannot be excluded. This ensures organization-wide instructions always apply regardless of individual settings."
current: No code path reads any instruction or memory file from a system directory, on either the legacy or the live route. Live route (every normal send): `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:880) has exactly three roots — global at :902-946 (CONFIG_DIR = `~/.nessy-agent`: MEMORY.md at :909, `rules/` at :921), workspace at :948-990 (`PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES` = ['AGENTS.md','CLAUDE.md','CLAUDE.local.md'] at :82, pushed at :987-990), and trusted project at :992-1116. The scope vocabulary is closed at four values: `CapabilityScopeKind = 'builtin' | 'global' | 'workspace' | 'project'` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/types.ts:31), mirrored on the wire as `SafeCapabilityScopeKind` (packages/shared/src/protocol/capabilities.ts:28) and ranked by `scopeSpecificity` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:863-869: project 3, workspace 2, global 1, builtin 0). Legacy route: packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:32 `CONTEXT_FILE_PATTERNS` = ['agents.md','claude.md','claude.local.md'] with scopes ent/project/local (:37-41), order ent/project/user/local (:42-47), plus one user-global `claude.md` (:36) from `getUserGlobalContextDirectory()` = `join(homeDir, '.nessy-agent')` (:136-138). The system directory IS already resolved in this fork, but for policy only: `managedPiPolicyPathForPlatform` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:44-51) returns `/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json`, `/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json`, `%ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json`, plus a `managed-policy.d/` drop-in dir (:62-67) — and none of the 34 keys in `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-533) carries instruction, memory or system-prompt content; the closest-named, `claudeRules` (:287), is permission-rule strings compiled into `permissionDsl`. packages/shared/src/config/managed-approval.ts:15-21 states the absence outright: "we carry no managed hook definitions and no managed instruction-file key". A NUL-safe `grep -a` for `ClaudeCode/CLAUDE`, `claude-code/CLAUDE`, `Nessy/CLAUDE`, `nessy/CLAUDE`, `Nessy/AGENTS`, `Nessy/MEMORY` over packages, apps, scripts returns zero code hits (only the divergence table itself). Two consequences follow: nothing can ever load an org-managed layer, and `instructionMemoryType` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:213-222) can never return its `'Managed'` value, because that arm is reached only from `scope.kind === 'builtin'` and no instruction/memory record is ever emitted at builtin scope (all pushes at native-sources.ts:899-1115 use globalScope/workspaceScope/projectScope; plugins cannot supply either kind — `grep -a` for `'instruction'`/`'memory'` across packages/shared/src/plugins returns zero, and both are native-only binding kinds at resolver.ts:897-900).
divergence: A whole tier is missing, not a misnamed key or a wrong value: the highest-authority, un-excludable memory scope has no reader. Everything the fix needs already exists and is unused for this purpose — (a) the system directory is already resolved per-platform for `managed-policy.json`, (b) the `builtin` scope kind already ranks 0 in `scopeSpecificity`, which is exactly memory.md:56's "broadest scope … loaded first" position for promptLayers (sorted by `order` at packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:253), and (c) `instructionMemoryType('builtin')` already returns the documented `'Managed'` memory_type. Second delta, inside the same mechanism: the single exclusion pass at native-sources.ts:1131-1133 applies `claudeMdExcludes`/`instructionExcludes` to EVERY instruction and memory record, so once a system tier exists it would be excludable — contradicting memory.md:336 — unless that filter carves it out.

change.what: New ~15-line helper in shared (native-sources.ts cannot import from server-core; the dependency runs the other way). Return the platform system directory that already holds the managed policy — `/Library/Application Support/Nessy` (darwin), `/etc/nessy` (linux), `join(process.env.ProgramData, 'Nessy')` (win32), `undefined` on anything else. Then make packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:44-51 `managedPiPolicyPathForPlatform` join `managed-policy.json` onto this helper instead of spelling the three paths a second time, so the policy file and the managed CLAUDE.md can never drift apart.

Add a `systemDir?: string` test seam to `NativeSourcesEnv` (:57-66, defaulting to `managedInstructionDirForPlatform()`), and insert a new `── Managed (system directory) ──` block immediately BEFORE the global block at :902, using `const managedScope: CapabilityScopeRef = { kind: 'builtin' }`. Push, in this order: `fileRecord('instruction', join(systemDir, name), managedScope, name)` for each of `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES` (:82) — CLAUDE.md is the documented name, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.local.md come free from the existing constant — and `memoryFileRecords(join(systemDir, 'MEMORY.md'), systemDir, managedScope, 'MEMORY.md', 'managed', seenMemoryFiles)`. Position matters twice: promptLayers are sorted by `order = scopeSpecificity(scope)` (resolver.ts:936, views.ts:253) and builtin is 0, so the layer lands first; memory layers are NOT sorted (views.ts has no `memory.sort`), so they keep push order and must be pushed before the global tier. Guard the read the way the policy loader guards its own file (managed-policy-loader.ts:76-82 `safeNode` + `assertPosixOwnerAndMode`: reject symlinks, require uid 0 and no group/other write on POSIX) — this tier cannot be turned off by the user, so a world-writable `/etc/nessy` must not become an instruction-injection channel. Then amend the exclusion filter at :1131-1133 to keep any record whose `scope.kind === 'builtin'`, per memory.md:336.

Two cases against `env.systemDir` pointed at a tmp dir: (1) a `CLAUDE.md` there produces one `kind:'instruction'`, `scope.kind:'builtin'` record that precedes every global/workspace/project instruction record in the returned array; (2) an `instructionExcludes` pattern matching that absolute path does NOT drop it, while the same pattern still drops a workspace CLAUDE.md — the memory.md:336 invariant. Add a negative case for the ownership guard if the harness can chown; otherwise assert the symlink rejection, which needs no root.

One case pinning that a managed-tier file reports `memory_type: 'Managed'` with `load_reason: 'session_start'` — the previously unreachable arm of `instructionMemoryType` (base-agent.ts:213-222). No production change needed here; the mapping already exists.

blastRadius: `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` is called from one production site, packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:641 inside `buildCapabilityResolutionInputsV2`, and its records flow through resolver → snapshot → `toAgentRuntime` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:150) into three consumers: `composePinnedCapabilityContext` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:960-1010, the pinned block and the `InstructionsLoaded` emission), the Pi harness manifest (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:368, which enumerates promptLayers+memory), the Pi context resource (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/context-resource.ts:63), and the child-session ceiling (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:187). Adding records changes the capability generation digest (resolver.ts:2258 `bindingGenerationMaterial` + key sort), which invalidates the pinned-context cache and re-emits `InstructionsLoaded` — expected, but it means every session re-sends the block once after the upgrade. Hook consumers begin seeing a `memory_type` value they have never received (`'Managed'`), which is a payload-content change on the hook boundary even though the type already admits it. Persistence keys already accept builtin scope, so nothing migrates: packages/shared/src/capabilities/policy-store.ts:103 and trust-store.ts:55 both normalize `'builtin' | 'global'` to a bare `{ kind }`. Renderer surfaces that render `scope.kind` will show these as builtin/`origin: 'builtin'` (resolver.ts:1667) — cosmetic, and the only reason to consider the heavier route. NO wire or schema change on the recommended route: `SafeCapabilityScopeKind` (packages/shared/src/protocol/capabilities.ts:28) is untouched. The alternative route — a fifth scope kind such as `'managed'` — DOES cross the wire boundary (protocol/capabilities.ts:28 plus types.ts:31, `scopeSpecificity`, `nativeResourceSource`, `instructionMemoryType`, policy-store/trust-store normalization, and every renderer scope label), which is a risk trigger in this repo; it buys only an honest label. Safe mode short-circuits before any of this (storage-runtime.ts:631 returns `SAFE_MODE_INPUTS`), so a managed layer is absent in safe mode — consistent with our own posture, worth a line in the plan.
userImpact: Latent for an individual user; immediate and silent for the first org that follows the page. A platform/IT team that deploys `CLAUDE.md` to the system directory — the same directory from which this fork already reads `managed-policy.json`, so the deployment channel is believed to work — gets no effect and no error: the org standards never enter the pinned capability block, no loaded-memory list mentions the file, and nothing reports that it was ignored. The only distribution channels left are per-user (`~/.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md`, `rules/`) or per-repo (`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`), and both are user-editable and excludable via `instructionExcludes`/`claudeMdExcludes` (native-sources.ts:1131-1133), so a compliance or security-policy instruction cannot be made to hold machine-wide. Secondary and testable today: any hook watching `InstructionsLoaded` can never observe `memory_type: 'Managed'`.
